title: Rigveda 2.40: To Soma and  Pusan
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 2.40: To Soma and  Pusan: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 2.40 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma and Pusan. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 2, the family book of Gṛtsamada. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 181r-181v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 2.40.1-2 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 181r
translation.original_text:
1somā̍pūṣaṇā̱ jana̍nā rayī̱ṇāṁ jana̍nā di̱vo jana̍nā pṛthi̱vyāḥ | jā̱tau viśva̍sya̱ bhuva̍nasya go̱pau de̱vā a̍kṛṇvann a̱mṛta̍sya̱ nābhi̍m ||
2i̱mau de̱vau jāya̍mānau juṣante̱mau tamā̍ṁsi gūhatā̱m aju̍ṣṭā | ā̱bhyām indra̍ḥ pa̱kvam ā̱māsv a̱ntaḥ so̍māpū̱ṣabhyā̍ṁ janad u̱sriyā̍su ||
translation.text:
1SOMA and Pûshan, Parents of all riches, Parents of earth and Parents of high heaven, You Twain, brought forth as the whole world's protectors, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.
2At birth of these two Gods all Gods are joyful: they have caused darkness, which we hate, to vanish. With these, with Soma and with Pûshan, Indra generates ripe warm milk in the raw milch-cows.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 181r (numbered 3r by the scribe) (OPenn image 182, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 2.39.5 ‹ā yātam arvāk hastau-iva›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 181v (numbered 3v by the scribe), begins in RV 2.40.3 ‹rajasaḥ vi-mānam sapta-cakram ratham›. Verses 2.40.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1somāpūṣaṇā | jananā | rayīṇām | jananā | divaḥ | jananā | pṛthivyāḥ | jātau | viśvasya | bhuvanasya | gopau | devāḥ | akṛṇvan | amṛtasya | nābhim
2imau | devau | jāyamānau | juṣanta | imau | tamāṃsi | gūhatām | ajuṣṭā | ābhyām | indraḥ | pakvam | āmāsu | antariti | somāpūṣa-bhyām | janat | usriyāsu

translation.original_ref: RV 2.40.3-6 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 181v
translation.original_text:
3somā̍pūṣaṇā̱ raja̍so vi̱māna̍ṁ sa̱ptaca̍kra̱ṁ ratha̱m avi̍śvaminvam | vi̱ṣū̱vṛta̱m mana̍sā yu̱jyamā̍na̱ṁ taṁ ji̍nvatho vṛṣaṇā̱ pañca̍raśmim ||
4di̱vy a1̱̍nyaḥ sada̍naṁ ca̱kra u̱ccā pṛ̍thi̱vyām a̱nyo adhy a̱ntari̍kṣe | tāv a̱smabhya̍m puru̱vāra̍m puru̱kṣuṁ rā̱yas poṣa̱ṁ vi ṣya̍tā̱ṁ nābhi̍m a̱sme ||
5viśvā̍ny a̱nyo bhuva̍nā ja̱jāna̱ viśva̍m a̱nyo a̍bhi̱cakṣā̍ṇa eti | somā̍pūṣaṇā̱v ava̍ta̱ṁ dhiya̍m me yu̱vābhyā̱ṁ viśvā̱ḥ pṛta̍nā jayema ||
6dhiya̍m pū̱ṣā ji̍nvatu viśvami̱nvo ra̱yiṁ somo̍ rayi̱pati̍r dadhātu | ava̍tu de̱vy adi̍tir ana̱rvā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
3Soma and Pûshan, urge your chariot hither, the seven-wheeIed car that measures out the region, That stirs not all, that moves to every quarter, fivc-reined and harnessed by the thought, ye Mighty.
4One in the heaven on high hath made his dwelling, on earth and in the firmament the other. May they disclose to us great store of treasure, much-longed for, rich in food, source of enjoyment.
5One of you Twain is Parent of all creatures, the otherjourneys onward all-beholding. Soma and Pûshan, aid my thought with favour: with you may we o'ercome in all encounters.
6May Pûshan stir our thought, the all-impelling, may Soma Lord of riches grant us riches. May Aditi the perfect Goddess aid us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
